challenge.better_approach: Considered adding the launch proof to the ground loop proof's sanctioned readers: that loosens a tooth whose why (one reader, named in cairn/devices/recovery/proofs/test_ground_loop_survives_its_caller.py line 71) the launch proof has no reason to break, and a tooth change needs a decision. Routing the read through the tool is the smaller and truer change.
challenge.hidden_assumption: That the scoped child can import cairn: it runs under scoped_exec with an unknown cwd, so _READ_MAX must insert the repo path itself, as the parent child string already does.
challenge.prior_art: Grepped CairnCommons tickets for test_ground_loop_survives_its_caller: c3b14029d6d8, d6eb399ab6ad, e179281f6eff, f04d5ef26a48. None owns this red; 60f16ffccd43 (PROVED) introduced the reader in its proof.
challenge.real_collision: None: 60f16ffccd43's why (the launch path's OS answers live in the system device) is untouched; only its proof's way of reading the cgroup changes.

answers.falsifier: test_ground_loop_survives_its_caller.py's 'exactly one file READS /proc/<pid>/cgroup from python' tooth is green; test_the_launch_tool_answers_the_launch_paths_os_questions.py's scoped-exec tooth still reads memory.max 100M
answers.from_idea: none, because it was measured, not imagined: cairn/devices/recovery/proofs/test_ground_loop_survives_its_caller.py reds on main with readers ['cairn/devices/system_rackmount/tools/launch/proofs/test_the_launch_tool_answers_the_launch_paths_os_questions.py', 'cairn/tools/cgroup/cgroup.py', 'cairn/tools/cgroup/proofs/test_cgroup.py'] (bin/cairn test over it, 2026-11-24)
answers.how: _READ_MAX in test_the_launch_tool_answers_the_launch_paths_os_questions.py puts the repo on sys.path and calls cairn.tools.cgroup.cgroup.cgroup_of() for the path it joins under /sys/fs/cgroup; no tooth changes. test_ground_loop_survives_its_caller.py is the red proof that turns green.
answers.traces_to: Law 9 (a red on main since 60f16ffccd43 landed, read by every PROVED gate over recovery) and RULE 1 (the read of /proc/<pid>/cgroup is the cgroup tool's, reached through its public interface)
answers.what: The launch tool's proof asks cairn/tools/cgroup for the scoped child's cgroup instead of reading /proc/self/cgroup itself, so cairn/tools/cgroup stays the sole reader the ground loop's proof holds it to.

bullets.text: 60f16ffccd43's proof spelled its own /proc/self/cgroup read, so the ground loop's sole-reader tooth has been red on main since it landed, blocking every PROVED over recovery
